lines: Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) for a Two-Year Funding Application Cycle

The City of Gilroy’s Housing and Community Services Division announces a virtual public hearing on the availability of federal Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funding through its Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) covering Program Years (PYs) 2027-2028 and 2028-2029.

Each year, the City receives approximately $400,000 in CDBG entitlement funding from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). Successful applications will be funded over a two-year period and the City will not release a NOFA for PY 2028-2029.

The CDBG Program is designed to support activities that (1) benefit low- and moderate-income persons, (2) aid in the prevention of slums or blight, and (3) meet an urgent community need. Through this NOFA, the City invites nonprofit organizations to apply for eligible activities that primarily benefit low- and moderate-income individuals or households earning no more than 80% of the area median income for Santa Clara County. All CDBG funds awarded through this NOFA must be used exclusively to assist City of Gilroy residents. Housing preservation is an eligible use of CDBG funds. HUD limits the amount of CDBG funding that may be used for public service activities to 15% of the City’s annual CDBG allocation. This NOFA covers a two-year funding cycle for the third and fourth program years of the City’s five-year Consolidated Plan (2025-2030).
Applications are due by 5:00 PM on January 7, 2027.

Funded activities must be carried out in PY 2027-2028 (July 1, 2027, through June 30, 2028) and PY 2028-2029 (July 1, 2028, through June 30, 2029), address at least one priority goal identified in the City’s 2025-2030 Consolidated Plan and comply with CDBG and City funding requirements outlined in the application packet.
(CDBG Application and Packet will be available here on December 2, 2026)
CDBG Program NOFA Public Hearing December 9, 2026

A virtual Public Hearing to obtain community input on housing and community development needs and priorities, proposed PY 2027-2028 and 2028-2029 NOFA programs and activities, and the grant application process will be held on: Wednesday, December 9, 2026, at 6:00 PM.

The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) provides annual grants on a formula basis to states, cities, and counties to develop viable urban communities by providing decent housing, a suitable living environment, and by expanding economic opportunities, principally for low - to moderate-income persons. The program is authorized under Title 1 of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974, Public Law 93-383, as amended 42 U.S.C. 5301 et seq.

Gilroy’s CDBG Program provides funding to eligible nonprofit organizations and City departments that administer programs, projects, and services that address the City’s priority housing and community development needs and primarily benefit low-income Gilroy residents. CDBG funds are typically awarded by the City through a competitive application process.

To receive CDBG funding, the City submits an Annual Action Plan (AAP) to HUD each year. Each AAP outlines the proposed use of CDBG funds and serves as one year of the City's five-year Consolidated Plan.

2025 - 2030 Consolidated Plan Including the 2025 - 2026 Annual Action Plan (AAP)

A five-year Consolidated Plan identifies local community development needs and sets forth a strategy to address these needs. The Consolidated Plan must address both affordable housing and non-housing-related community development needs. The needs are targeted to low-income persons or low-income areas. By May 15 of each year, the City submits an Annual Action Plan to HUD as part of its five-year Consolidated Plan, describing the proposed use of CDBG funds.
